source.title: Continued Pretraining of FinBERT on Finnish Histopathological Reports: Train-Time Signals and Proxy Downstream Correlations
source.authors: R. Luisto; Liisa Petäinen; Tommi Grönholm; J. Böhm; M. Ahtiainen; Tomi Lilja; I. Pölönen; S. Äyrämö

record.tranche_reason: The study reports exploratory correlations between CPT loss changes and proxy classification improvement, bearing on V6. It also uses scaling laws as a qualitative interpretive lens, but does not fit or test them.
record.gate_note: The authors explicitly say they do not fit power laws. The CPT loss curves and best validation losses are reported by corpus, not as a scaling sweep that tests a power-law form, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. The exploratory correlation between relative CPT train-loss improvement and classification improvement bears on V6. Other cited scaling-law results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study does not fit, extrapolate or compare scaling laws. It uses the Hoffmann loss form only as a qualitative lens for interpreting CPT loss curves of one fixed FinBERT model, stating 'We will not be fitting our train-time observations to such power laws.' Its one quantitative link between loss and downstream performance (r1) correlates the relative drop in CPT training loss with proxy classification gains across 9 corpora. That is a domain-adaptation construct with a fixed model, training rather than held-out loss, and no scale axis. The correlation was picked post hoc from 91 features × 129 targets. It is not a measure of downstream performance improving with scale or pretraining loss as V6 names, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find CPT loss curves differ strongly by corpus familiarity: flat for YLE, which was in the pretraining data, and steep drops for Histopathology and Finlex. Their exploratory, post hoc analysis finds tentative associations between CPT signals (loss-curve geometry, layerwise embedding change, isotropy) and proxy classification gains. They state none of the findings are statistically established and that the findings were in line with expectations. They call for replication and for 'capped power laws for CPT'.
record.recipe_differences: This is domain-specific continued pretraining of one fixed FinBERT model, with loss curves and exploratory downstream correlations; it does not reproduce the original parameter/data/compute scaling sweeps or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Corpus/domain familiarity changes the reported CPT loss-curve behavior; YLE showed little change, while Finlex and Histopathology showed drastic change.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 9 labeled Finnish corpora, the relative drop in CPT training loss correlates with the logistic-regression macro-F1 error-reduction rate (r = 0.961, ρ = 0.800). The feature-target pair was chosen post hoc from 91 features × 129 targets, with no multiple-comparison correction. Final train loss correlates negatively with targets (about −0.4 to −0.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In continued pretraining of a fixed model, the size of the domain loss drop predicts frozen-embedding downstream gains across domains.

fits_no_version.finding: CPT training-loss curves barely move on corpora seen in pretraining (YLE) and drop sharply on novel domains (Finlex, Histopathology). The authors read this through L(D)=C+BD^−β without fitting it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CPT loss reduction scales with domain novelty relative to the original pretraining data.

record.problems: The authors describe the downstream-correlation analysis as exploratory and post hoc; features and targets were selected from 91 features and 129 targets without multiple-comparison correction. The labeled correlations use nine dataset variants, and the authors state that findings are not statistically established and need replication. The CPT loss curves are not fitted to power laws.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss to parameters, tokens or compute; fixed model, CPT loss curves only interpreted qualitatively.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
Domain CPT loss curves are shown but no power-law form is fitted or tested for CPT/transfer.
No downstream performance measured across model scale or as a function of pretraining loss level; only an exploratory cross-corpus correlation of CPT loss drop with proxy gains.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents; no test of bending away from a power law.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's test of V6 and its supports/limits_scope labels are withdrawn. The study never varies scale, and its loss–downstream link is a cross-domain CPT correlation, not V6's relation. The scaling-law content is purely interpretive. Rows r2–r23 are correctly linked to none.

versions.untested_parts: No test of a power-law fit to held-out pretraining loss over parameters, tokens, or compute; fixed model and CPT setting.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute search or comparison of parameter and token allocations.
No comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count.
Finnish-language text CPT is studied, but no test of whether a power-law form transfers across modalities or training regimes.

Tests an exploratory association between relative CPT train-loss improvement and proxy classification improvement; does not test scaling-based prediction, downstream performance across model scale, or prediction from absolute pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents or fitting choices, and no test of curves bending away from a fitted power law.

rows.subject: FinBERT and continued-pretrained FinBERT
rows.operation_detail: Correlated relative CPT train-loss improvement with proxy classification improvement across labeled dataset variants.
rows.measure: Pearson and Spearman correlation between train-loss relative improvement and logistic-regression macro-F1 error-reduction rate
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI shown in Figure 5(a), exact values not stated
rows.note: Aggregate association across dataset variants, not a model-scale sweep or a prospective prediction. The authors call the analysis exploratory and post hoc.
rows.check: Measures a cross-corpus correlation between relative CPT train-loss drop and logistic-regression macro-F1 ERR for one fixed model (n=9). There is no scale variation, the loss is training rather than held-out pretraining loss, and the pair was selected post hoc from 91×129 comparisons without correction. This is not V6's scale-to-downstream or pretraining-loss-to-downstream relation. Relinked to none and moved to fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CPT relative loss improvement versus logistic-regression macro-F1 error-reduction rate across the 9 labeled dataset variants, with 500 training samples
reader_labels.reason: The reported association is strong (r = 0.961; ρ = 0.800), consistent with a relationship between a CPT loss signal and proxy downstream improvement; see r1.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Exploratory post-hoc analysis across the tested labeled dataset variants
reader_labels.reason: The authors selected features and targets from many comparisons, applied no multiple-comparison correction, and describe the associations as tentative rather than established; see r1.
